op1: 1.  Dismisses unanimously the Government’s preliminary objection and holds that the applicant can claim to be a “victim” for the purposes of Article 34 of the Convention;
op2: 2.  Holds by sixteen votes to one that there has been no violation of Article 8 of the Convention in respect of application no. 4149/04;
op3: 3.  Holds by sixteen votes to one that there has been no violation of Article 8 of the Convention in respect of application no. 41029/04;
op4: In accordance with Article 45 § 2 of the Convention and Rule 74 § 2 of the Rules of Court, the separate opinion of Judge Gyulumyan is annexed to this judgment.
p11: 11.  In the introduction, the author continued as follows:
p12: 12.  One chapter of the book was devoted to “Gypsies in present-day Turkey”. It contained the following passages:
p13: 13.  The final paragraphs of the conclusion of the book “The Gypsies in Turkey” read as follows:
p14: 14.  On 15 June 2001 the applicant, acting on behalf of the Turkish Gypsy/Roma associations, submitted a request to the Ministry of Culture in which he explained that the author of the impugned book accused Gypsies of engaging in illegal activities, described them as “thieves, pickpockets, swindlers, robbers, usurers, beggars, drug dealers, prostitutes and brothel keepers” and portrayed them as polygamous and aggressive. The applicant also asserted that the book contained several other expressions which were humiliating and debasing for Gypsies. Alleging that these expressions were punishable under the criminal law, he requested that sales of the book be halted and that all copies of it be seized.
p15: 15.  On the same day the head of the publications unit of the Ministry of Culture ordered his unit to return the remaining 299 copies of the book.
